review: Reviewed both runtime deltas against the public preview, full worker parser/dispatcher, provider handoff validation and dispatch/receipt surroundings, changed test fixtures/cases and relay-correlation suite. Provider item ID is submitted separately from event ID for transcript correlation.

Existing candidate adds a governed Minecraft command dispatch kind. Client requires a room handoff, explicit server admission, exactly the Minecraft command capability, worker-required action-candidate status, no goal binding and consistent action/read-only flags. Provider tool execution, workstation mutation, assistant answer and terminal authority remain forbidden.

Dispatch launches the backend Ask entrypoint with workstation payload actions suppressed. It does not execute a game action or establish owner, room, world, actor, expiry or consent authority. Those remain server/adapter checks. Ordinary action candidates continue through read-only reasoning; provider tool-call events are ignored.

Added twelve negative client cases for personal scope, missing admission, goal/session attachment, additional capability, non-action/parallel outcome, provider-tool permission, inconsistent action/read-only flags, runtime mismatch and missing tool prohibition. These checks use synthetic server replies and preserve the original runtime implementation.

Existing suite covers personal voice destinations, missing attribution, disposed handlers, local/parallel/goal/read-only paths, playback settlement, interruption, missing receipts, rejected runtime, retry and deduplication. Relay checks distinguish provider event/item IDs and correlate terminal response/playback receipts. No actual provider transcript or credentials are exported.
limits: Unfrozen unpublished source proposal. This cohort adds tests only to canonical source; it exports existing runtime changes without modifying their admission policy. No installed behavior is newly established.

Mocked server responses cannot prove real authentication, exact room/world/player authorization, consent, revocation, server validation of routed metadata, or game execution. The matching server and adapter checks and attended Minecraft/GPT Live handoff remain required.

Export tests execute the two selected exported runtime modules with canonical shared contracts and other dependencies. Selected compilation is not a standalone app build or complete typecheck. Shared-contract publication is a separately inventoried repository.
No Codex chat message, pairing change, model run, microphone access, room mutation or game action occurred. No physical viability, certificate integrity or release-readiness claim is made.
Five intentional support-contact matches elsewhere remain in final owner publication review. Larger Console integration and ordinary-account signed acceptance remain open.
